keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area; the Perm Krai (about 160,000 km2) is my reading of the described basin and runs somewhat south of the Chusovaya confluence. Its Pechora and Urals limits match the page.

ledger.note: 1451: Vasily II appoints Mikhail Yermolayevich prince of Great Perm. The page's lead names the 'Principality of Perm (1451-1505)' and says 'In 1451, Vasily II appointed Mikhail Yermolayevich as the prince of Great Perm'; the land stays 'formally dependent on Novgorod until 1471'.

region.text: the upper Kama: bounded by the Pechora River and Lake Chusovskoye in the north, the Chusovaya confluence in the south, the Kama's source in the west and the Urals in the east (page, paraphrased), with Cherdyn as 'the center of the region'

ledger.note: 1472: Ivan III invades Great Perm. 'In 1472, Ivan III dispatched Fyodor Paletsky for a campaign against Great Perm'; his forces defeated the Komi-Permyak forces and founded Pokcha (page, paraphrased). Novgorod 'formally gave up its rights in 1471'.
1472: the seat moves from Cherdyn to the newly founded Pokcha (infobox 'Pokcha (1472-1535)').

region.text: the upper Kama: bounded by the Pechora River and Lake Chusovskoye in the north, the Chusovaya confluence in the south, the Kama's source in the west and the Urals in the east (page, paraphrased), with Cherdyn as 'the center of the region'

ledger.note: 1472: Paletsky's campaign ends the fighting: his forces defeated the Komi-Permyak forces and founded Pokcha, 'a stronghold for Moscow' (the page). Reviewer eu-16-x moved this from 1478: the page's 'ultimately annexed by Moscow in 1478' is said of Novgorod ('Novgorod ... formally gave up its rights in 1471 before it was ultimately annexed by Moscow in 1478'), not of Great Perm, which the page has dependent on Moscow after 1471 and incorporated in 1505.

notes: New state of the Rus colonial fringe (not flagged by a sibling; found while checking the scope's Siberian advance and Novgorod's northern land). One page (page budget; the article is short). The page's dates conflict: infobox Established 1324 / Disestablished 1708 (the wider Perm Land), lead 'Principality of Perm (1451-1505)', 1478 (Novgorod's annexation, not Perm's: reviewer eu-16-x), 1505 final incorporation. The dossier takes the lead's 1451-1505. Novgorod's dossier (eu-16-b) has no matching 1471 event (its gap lists the north as undated). Cherdyn and Pokcha are missing from the gazetteer (gazetteer_names_needed). Wikidata id unknown.
